title: Bank CEOs, NSA Tell Congress That AI-Driven Patches Are Behind Outages - Slashdot
excerpt: An anonymous reader quotes a report from The Washington Sun: Wall Street executives and the National Security Agency have told members of Congress that this week's widespread tech outages were caused by attempts to fix vulnerabilities identified by artificial intelligence, according to three sources...
content_html:
An anonymous reader quotes a report from The Washington Sun: Wall Street executives and the National Security Agency have told members of Congress that this week's widespread tech outages were caused by attempts to fix vulnerabilities identified by artificial intelligence, according to three sources familiar with the private conversations. [...] "These models are identifying massive vulnerabilities, and that increases the urgency to patch right away," said one congressional official briefed on the matter. "They're trying to push through a lot of patches all at once -- more than the system was designed for."

On Monday, banks such as JP Morgan Chase blamed software-related bugs for the service issues. On Tuesday, the NSA said that "scheduled routine maintenance" was responsible for the "temporary degradation" of some of its networks. Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin told CNBC on Tuesday that "they're pushing new technology on top of really old computer systems, and it just seems to overwhelm the system. ... We're going to see more of this as new technology rolls out."

"There's some sense in which this is reassuring, in that it means there's not an attack. But it shows the extent to which safety critical infrastructure we rely on is based on software with large vulnerabilities on legacy systems," said Nathan Calvin, the chief strategy officer at Encode. "Updating those is going to be a rocky process, and as we get more advanced models this won't be a one and done thing -- we'll continue to find more vulnerabilities."
